articles.title: Republican-aligned actors issued nearly three-quarters of fact-checked 2024 election hoaxes
articles.summary: During the 2024 U.S. presidential election, politicians and anonymous users openly used disinformation as a campaign strategy. A new study reveals who spread these hoaxes, how they shared them, and who was targeted by the fabricated claims.

articles.title: Problematic pornography use is linked to craving, shame, depression, and loneliness, meta-analysis finds
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 121,728 participants finds that problematic pornography use is most strongly linked to craving and sexual shame, with smaller links to depression and loneliness. How strong these links appear may depend on the measure used.

articles.title: Women and underrepresented minorities have higher tenure-track placement rates in the political science job market
articles.summary: What actually lands a PhD student a tenure-track professorship? A new study suggests a candidate's publication record, research field, and demographic identity are much stronger predictors of hiring success than the prestige of their university.

articles.title: New study links sexual objectification at home to young women’s difficulty saying no to unwanted sex
articles.summary: New research suggests that young women who received objectifying messages from their families growing up are more likely to view themselves as objects, a mindset linked to difficulties communicating sexual desires and experiencing orgasm.

articles.title: Virtual reality can induce mystical experiences, new study suggests
articles.summary: Virtual reality headsets might offer a reliable way to induce profound feelings of unity and awe typically associated with deep spiritual practices or psychedelics, providing researchers with a new tool to study human consciousness.

articles.title: Study of 2.5 million children finds no link between MMR vaccine and autism
articles.summary: Evaluating the health records of over 2.5 million children, researchers found no evidence that receiving the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine before age two increases the risk of a childhood autism diagnosis.

articles.title: This diet may slow brain aging by 2.5 years
articles.summary: People who followed the MIND diet more closely showed slower brain shrinkage and less grey matter loss over time, with the strongest differences equivalent to about 2.5 years of delayed brain aging. Berries and poultry were linked with healthier brain changes, while sweets and fried fast foods were associated with greater tissue loss.

articles.title: Could quitting ultra-processed food boost your mental health?
articles.summary: People with depression who dramatically cut ultra-processed foods experienced notable improvements in their symptoms in a small preliminary study. Researchers suspect healthier eating may benefit the brain partly by reducing gut damage and chronic inflammation.

articles.title: Children at risk for depression get “stuck” on sad faces
articles.summary: Depression may change which emotional faces children notice most, but the pattern appears to depend on family history. Children at higher familial risk became increasingly focused on sad faces, while lower-risk children with rising symptoms paid less attention to happy ones.

articles.title: Brain scans reveal which disorders are linked to faster brain aging
articles.summary: A massive MRI study found that Alzheimer’s disease, mild cognitive impairment, psychiatric disorders, and addiction are associated with distinct patterns of accelerated brain aging. The strongest effects appeared in Alzheimer’s and mild cognitive impairment, while ADHD and autism showed no significant overall difference.

articles.title: Scientists just discovered what coffee really does to your gut and brain
articles.summary: A new study suggests coffee may influence mood and brain function by changing the activity of microbes in the gut. Both caffeinated and decaf coffee were linked to lower stress, depression, and impulsivity, while also producing measurable changes in gut bacteria and metabolites. Decaf was associated with better learning and memory, while caffeinated coffee appeared to reduce anxiety and improve attention.
